text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- North Korean Deputy Prime Minister Kong Jin-tae arrives in Vietnam on Monday for a week-long visit.
-- State firm PetroVietnam and Malaysia's Petronas will start joint exploitation of an oil field in waters where the two countries have overlapaping territorial claims within the next three months.
-- Vietnam expects to mobilize some $8 million for development this year through a planned stock exchange transaction unit.
-- Vietnam plans to invest $3.3 billion in a power station in the northern province of Son La. Some 90,000 people will be moved to make way for construction.
-- The Prime Minister has asked high-ranking local officials to take part in a course on administrative management.
-- 8,800 criminal cases were uncovered and 967 criminal rings destroyed in Vietnam during the last three months.
-- U.S Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin arrived in Hanoi on Sunday for a three-day official visit.
-- The Prime Minister has issued a directive aimed at tightening controls over the treatment of industrial waste.
-- Ho Chi Minh City expects an average annual growth rate of 12.6 percent between 1997 and 2010.
